name: Zozulia

placement_rationale.text: Unlike a near-line strike drone, Zozulia is a one-way-attack airframe with no return flight, so 1,050 km represents a confirmed/typical strike depth into Russian territory rather than a launch-site offset from the front — the crew and launch rail sit inside Ukraine, far outside this figure. 1,050 km sits almost exactly halfway between the two ranges this asset's own characteristics report — ~1,000 km carrying a 50 kg warhead and ~2,100 km with a lighter, unstated payload — a conservative reading rather than the maximum claimed reach. This extends doctrine.md §2's 10–150+ km medium/long-range strike layer into the deep_strategic band the same way the Spiderweb entry documents for cross-border reach generally: once the delivery is a mass-producible airframe, distance alone stops being a reliable defensive factor.

Strength: Longest reported range of any Ukrainian long-range strike drone in this catalog - a direct range/payload trade-off choice favoring reach over warhead size
Limitation: Very new (2025 reveal), so combat track record and reliability are less established than older types like Beaver or FP-1
Estimated quantity available: Newly introduced; production scale not yet disclosed
employment_notes: Represents the newest and longest-reaching type in Ukraine's deep-strike drone family, continuing the trend of each successive domestic design pushing range further into Russian territory
contrast_vs_traditional: An extreme-range one-way attack drone is the clearest version of the doctrine.md point made explicit for cross-border strikes: once the delivery method is a mass-producible airframe rather than a missile, distance from the front stops being a reliable protective factor at all, for targets that traditional doctrine treated as safely out of reach.
